# /cc-nexs:git-custodian

Only the Orchestrator may invoke this command. Implementation, review, and verification roles must not run branch, merge, push, worktree-removal, or branch-deletion commands. No session, the Orchestrator included, merges, rebases, or pulls a test branch into a feature branch; feature branches take only the configured base, and test conflicts go through `/cc-nexs:resolve-test-conflict`.

Load `.cc-nexs/workspace.yml` with `loadWorkspaceConfig()` and use `git-custodian.mjs`. After create, persist each returned `baseBranch` and `baseCommit` in progress.json. Later prepare/cleanup actions use that recorded base branch and fail if the workspace mapping changed unexpectedly.

- `reserve`: Lean only. Call `publishDocsReservation()` before their code worktrees are created. Hotfix never invokes this action. This is the sole narrow exception that may commit and fast-forward push directly to the docs base: it may only create a previously absent `doc/<id>.<slug>/README.md` and `.cc-nexs-reservation.json`; it may never edit existing paths, force-push, or fall back to a local-only number. This phase-one commit makes the number visible to developers who do not use cc-nexs.
- `create`: Hotfix is initialized through `init-hotfix`: create `hotfix/<key>` and `.worktrees/<key>/<repo>/` from configured remote bases without a feature reservation or placeholder push. For Lean, fetch the configured remote base, then create one same-named feature branch with no upstream and one isolated worktree per selected repository under `.worktrees/<id>-<slug>/<repo-id>/`. Never branch from the caller's current checkout. Pre-G1 implementation sync may request `recoverExisting` only to close a crash between worktree creation and progress persistence; recovery requires the exact registered path/branch, a clean tree, and a HEAD that is still an ancestor of the configured remote base. A partial path/branch pair or any implementation commit fails closed.
- `candidate`: stage only explicitly declared paths and call `commitCandidate(..., progressFile)`. Candidate identity is written to progress.json **before** the commit with `commit: null`; the immutable `refs/cc-nexs/candidates/<feature>/<repo>` ref is the commit authority. Never write the resulting SHA back into progress.json, because that creates an uncommittable self-reference and leaves the docs worktree dirty forever. Test release resolves and freezes that ref before mutation, then rejects any ref movement observed during integration.
- Automatic `sync_base` uses `prepareFeatureForMerge` with `preserveConflicts: true`. Returned conflicts remain in the assigned development worktree for the Developer to resolve without Git mutation. Custodian then stages only resolved paths, checks that no unmerged entries remain, preserves the staged upstream merge, commits with the resolved repository identity, and advances the candidate ref. Do not call `commitCandidate` on the pending merge. Never edit or resolve conflicts on the shared base branch. A resolvable conflict is not a request for human intervention.
- `prepare`: only for explicitly required conflict/dependency resolution before a new candidate is verified, call `prepareFeatureForMerge()`. It fetches latest `origin/<base>`, requires a clean worktree, merges the latest base into the feature branch without rewriting published history, and advances the candidate ref. Do not run this on a tested/approved candidate merely because base advanced. Lean/Hotfix release-base integrates the unchanged candidate directly; ordinary candidate commits never run `git pull`.
- `cleanup`: local-only maintenance. Run after merge proof to remove the worktree, local feature branch, and candidate ref while retaining any remote feature branch. Use this only when the user has not authorized a complete release merge.
- `reclaim`: workspace-wide local cleanup. Run `node <plugin-root>/lib/cc-nexs-cli.mjs reclaim-worktrees [--sizes]` to show the plan and its confirmation token, present it to the user, and only after the user confirms run it again with `--confirm <token>`. The controller recomputes the plan and refuses if anything changed, re-fetches each base and re-proves the merge before removing a worktree, its local branch, and candidate ref. The same plan covers `.cc-nexs/runtime/verify/`: scratch left by attempts that are no longer running, and whole attempt records once their task is complete. It also covers `.cc-nexs/runtime/tasks/<id>/` once the task is complete, and dependency/build caches (`node_modules`, `.next` and similar) inside legacy `.cc-nexs/drafts/<task>/` directories of complete tasks; other draft content and Git checkouts are only reported. Three more kinds are covered so a waiting task does not hold the disk: the idle `scratch/` of an active task's files (one day; also removed without confirmation by the `verify-local` preflight), a clean worktree no task owns once idle for seven days (the worktree goes, its branch stays), and directories agents created beside the managed ones (under `.cc-nexs/runtime/` once their task is complete or after seven idle days; directly under `.cc-nexs/` only once their task is complete, otherwise reported with their age). A task idle for two weeks is reported with a `reconcile` hint. Running attempts, dirty source, and the logs of active tasks stay. An unmerged branch reports how many commits are patch-equivalent in the base. Progress from a retired mode still counts as an active task. Remote branches are never deleted: leftover `cc-nexs-mr-*` branches from releases before 0.11.0 are listed with their merge status for manual removal. Locked copies are reported as failed and left for a later run.
- `reconcile`: for a task whose work reached its bases outside the controller (a retired mode, a manual merge), run `node <plugin-root>/lib/cc-nexs-cli.mjs reconcile <id>`. It fetches each base and proves every assigned code repository's candidate, or branch commits beyond the recorded base, are contained by ancestry or as equivalent patches. Present the plan to the user and only after confirmation rerun with `--confirm <token>` to record `COMPLETE`. Unproven work blocks it; it never archives docs or deletes branches.
- `finalize`: when the user explicitly asks to merge/push to `master` or otherwise authorizes release, call `finalizeMergedWorktree()` for every code repository first and the docs repository last. A Lean/Hotfix release does this through its controllers: `release-base` cleans code repositories after proof and `finalize-docs` cleans the docs repository. It fetches both remote refs, proves the remote feature tip is reachable from the remote base, deletes the remote feature branch, then removes the local worktree, local feature branch, and candidate ref. Remote retention requires an explicit user instruction such as `--keep-remote`; it is no longer the default for an authorized merge. Leaving any local or remote feature branch behind is a failed release lifecycle.

For Lean, the docs repository uses two phases. Phase one is the constrained reservation commit above. Phase two follows the normal candidate protocol: during release, merge code repositories first, write their actual integration commit ids into the final docs artifacts if needed, then run `node <plugin-root>/lib/cc-nexs-cli.mjs finalize-docs <id>` to create, integrate, and clean the docs candidate last; rerun it while it reports `pending`. The number is already visible on the shared docs base throughout development.

New Hotfix docs have no reservation phase. Their single final docs candidate contains only the assigned BUG document; machine state remains under `.cc-nexs/hotfixes/<key>/`. Legacy tasks keep their existing archive layout. In-place Lean promotion uses the original branch and the BUG-adjacent `<BUGstem>.lean/` directory without allocating a number.

Remote branch deletion is never inferred from `COMPLETE` alone. It is inferred from the user's explicit authorization to merge/push the feature into the configured base. After that merge succeeds, finalize performs complete local and remote cleanup unless the user explicitly asks to retain the remote branch.

Before any role dispatch, follow `<plugin-root>/rules/model-discovery.md` and the shared `modelGateway` protocol: inspect cached choices, prepare a non-blocking preview, start immediately without waiting for a reply, and record the actual result. Apply real user corrections before start or to the next batch; never restart a running role merely to change models. This applies to the current runtime, including Claude-native single-step commands.
